description: Design a basic Automatic Repeat reQuest (ARQ) error correction system. The system should include a sender that transmits data frames and a receiver that checks for errors using a simple parity bit. If an error is detected, the receiver sends a request for retransmission of the frame. The sender should retry sending the frame upon receiving a retransmission request. The sender should have a maximum of 3 attempts to send the frame before giving up.
code:
module ARQ (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [7:0] data_in,
    input send,       
    output reg [7:0] data_out,
    output reg error,
    output reg request,
    input ack
);
    reg [2:0] attempt_count;
    reg [7:0] current_data;
    reg parity;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            attempt_count <= 0;
            request <= 0;
            error <= 0;
            data_out <= 0;
        end else begin
            if (send) begin
                current_data <= data_in;
                parity <= ^current_data; // Calculate parity
                data_out <= {current_data, parity}; // Send data with parity
                attempt_count <= attempt_count + 1;
                request <= 0; // No request initially
            end
            
            if (ack) begin
                if (parity == 1'b1) begin // If parity bit is 1, no error
                    attempt_count <= 0; // Reset on successful reception
                    request <= 0;
                end else begin
                    error <= 1; // Error detected
                    request <= 1; // Request retransmission
                end
            end
            
            if (attempt_count >= 3) begin
                // Handle maximum retry
                attempt_count <= 0; // Reset attempt count
                request <= 0; // Stop requests after max attempts
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

module uart_transmitter (
    input clk,               // Clock signal
    input start,             // Start signal
    input [7:0] data_in,     // 8-bit data input
    output reg tx,           // Serial output
    output reg busy          // Indicates if the transmitter is busy
);

    reg [3:0] bit_index;     // Index for which bit is being sent
    reg [7:0] data;          // Register to hold data
    reg [15:0] clk_div;      // Clock divider for baud rate
    parameter BAUD_RATE_DIV = 16; // Adjust this for desired baud rate

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (start && !busy) begin
            busy <= 1;       // Set busy flag
            data <= data_in; // Load data to send
            bit_index <= 0;  // Reset bit index
            tx <= 0;         // Start bit (active low)
            clk_div <= 0;    // Reset clock divider
        end else if (busy) begin
            clk_div <= clk_div + 1;
            if (clk_div == BAUD_RATE_DIV) begin
                clk_div <= 0; // Reset clock divider
                if (bit_index < 8) begin
                    tx <= data[bit_index]; // Send data bits
                    bit_index <= bit_index + 1; // Move to next bit
                end else begin
                    tx <= 1; // Stop bit (inactive state)
                    busy <= 0; // Clear busy flag after sending
                end
            end
        end
    end

endmodule

    input reset,
    input [7:0] data_in,        // Data input

    output reg [1:0] state      // State of the system
);

    reg [1:0] packet_counter;    // To keep track of sent packets
    parameter IDLE = 2'b00, SEND = 2'b01, WAIT_ACK = 2'b10, RETRANSMIT = 2'b11;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            packet_counter <= 0;
            data_out <= 0;

                        data_out <= data_in; // Send data
                        packet_counter <= packet_counter + 1;

                    if (ack) begin
                        state <= IDLE; // If ack received, go back to idle
                    end else begin
                        state <= RETRANSMIT; // If no ack, retransmit
                    end
                end

                RETRANSMIT: begin
                    data_out <= data_in; // Retransmit data

description:
Design a simple Kalman filter module in Verilog that fuses position and velocity measurements from a sensor. The filter will use a set of matrices for state prediction and measurement update. The input to the module will be the position measurement (z), velocity measurement (v), and the time step (dt). The output will be the estimated position and velocity (x_est and v_est). The Kalman filter equations used are:
1. Prediction: 
   - x_pred = A * x + B * u
   - P_pred = A * P * A' + Q
2. Update:
   - K = P_pred * H' * (H * P_pred * H' + R)^-1
   - x_est = x_pred + K * (z - H * x_pred)
   - P_est = (I - K * H) * P_pred
Where:
- A is the state transition matrix
- B is the control input matrix
- H is the measurement matrix
- Q is the process noise covariance
- R is the measurement noise covariance
- I is the identity matrix
code:
module kalman_filter (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [15:0] z, // Position measurement
    input [15:0] v, // Velocity measurement
    input [15:0] dt, // Time step
    output reg [15:0] x_est, // Estimated position
    output reg [15:0] v_est // Estimated velocity
);

// State variables
reg [15:0] x_pred;
reg [15:0] v_pred;
reg [15:0] P; // Estimate covariance
reg [15:0] K; // Kalman gain

// Constants for Kalman filter
parameter [15:0] A = 16'h0001; // Transition matrix (1)
parameter [15:0] H = 16'h0001; // Measurement matrix (1)
parameter [15:0] Q = 16'h0001; // Process noise covariance
parameter [15:0] R = 16'h0001; // Measurement noise covariance

always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
    if (rst) begin
        x_est <= 16'h0000;
        v_est <= 16'h0000;
        P <= 16'h0001; // Initial covariance
    end else begin
        // Prediction step
        x_pred <= A * x_est + v * dt; // Simple position prediction
        v_pred <= v; // Velocity prediction stays the same

        // Update step
        K <= P * H / (H * P * H + R); // Calculate Kalman gain
        x_est <= x_pred + K * (z - H * x_pred); // Update estimated position
        P <= (16'h0001 - K * H) * P; // Update the covariance
    end
end

endmodule
